# Candidate crystals
- Crystal-K2: inorganic scintillator, high light yield, fast decay.
- Crystal-K3: inorganic scintillator, medium light yield.
- Crystal-K1: inorganic scintillator, mature growth process, lower light yield.
All three are available in the required sizes from at least one vendor.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, nominal 5 cm thickness)
Energy resolution at 662 keV (FWHM): Crystal-K2 2.9%, Crystal-K3 4.5%, Crystal-K1 8.5%.
Thickness dependence was weak in the 3-8 cm range.

# Radiopurity assay campaign, Q1 2026
Sample crystals of each candidate were counted for 30 days in the underground HPGe station.
Intrinsic background of the crystal, 100-3000 keV (counts/kg/day):
- Crystal-K2: 2.0 +- 0.2   (dominated by internal contamination of the crystal itself)
- Crystal-K3: 0.30 +- 0.05
- Crystal-K1: 0.10 +- 0.03
Facility background budget for the spectrometer crystal: 0.5 counts/kg/day.
Contact: radiopurity working group.

# Meeting notes 2026-02-11
Attendees discussed the shielding upgrade (lead + copper, complete) and the schedule for commissioning in Q3. Action: finalise the crystal choice this quarter.

# Shielding status
The 20 cm lead + 5 cm OFHC copper castle is installed. Radon purge with boil-off nitrogen is operational.

content.text: K2 is ruled out by the background budget (2.0 vs 0.5 counts/kg/day). K1 and K3 both pass. Next I'll simulate their resolution across thicknesses.
K3 looks best near 5 cm. I'll check a couple of nearby thicknesses to locate the minimum more precisely.

input.justification: Crystal-K2 is excluded by the hard background constraint: its assayed intrinsic background is 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day (100–3000 keV), four times the 0.5 budget. Of the two remaining candidates, K1 has the lowest background (0.10) but poor resolution (8.4% at 5 cm, 10.4% at 2 cm, 12.6% at 10 cm). K3 has background 0.30 ± 0.05, which is within budget, and gives much better resolution. Scanning K3 thickness with the simulation gave FWHM of 4.97% (2 cm), 4.74% (3 cm), 4.48% (4 cm), 4.63% (5 cm), 4.57% (6 cm) and 6.37% (10 cm). The optimum is at about 4 cm, with 4.48% FWHM at 662 keV. Because the 2025 summary used a nominal 5 cm crystal, these values come from the new simulation runs.
